answers.answer: Shuffle all four III cards and place them face down at the bottom; shuffle all nine II and deal five face down above them; shuffle all three I and deal one face down on top. Return the unused I and II cards to the box unseen.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘shuffle ... deal’ tier instructions; unused cards return unseen.

answers.answer: Both player counts start at 0 VP in a three-player game and at 1 VP in a four-player game. In either count, humans start with two Agents on the Leader and a third (Swordmaster) beside the board; three troops in their nearest garrison and nine in supply; and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup: score marker is on 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; Agents, troops and water setup.

answers.answer: Yes, you may Reveal while Agents remain, but once you Reveal you are skipped for the rest of Player Turns and cannot take a later Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards remaining in hand and revealed then; Agent-turn cards use their Agent boxes, not Reveal boxes. At Clean Up, all cards in front of you from Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Agent turns optional; after Reveal turns skipped; Reveal Cards / Resolve Reveal Effects / Clean Up.

answers.answer: A legal Plot Intrigue played before placing your Agent can grant resources that pay the entry cost. Resources gained after placement from the destination or the played Agent card cannot pay that same cost; the entry cost must be paid immediately before resolving either. One card chooses only one Agent icon and sends one Agent. A card with no Agent icon cannot be used on an Agent turn; it can only be revealed.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot before placement; pay before effects; one Agent icon; no-Agent-icon restriction.

answers.answer: At a Combat space, deploy all three troops recruited that turn plus up to two more from the garrison, for five total in this example. At a non-Combat space you cannot normally deploy units. Recruited troops come from your supply and are placed in your garrison before deployment; the up-to-two additional units come from the garrison.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: recruit from supply; at Combat deploy current-turn recruits plus up to two from garrison.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon on the played card lets you send an Agent to a board space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy; you do not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy at a connected post to bypass another player's Agent on the destination, not your own Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy when you send an Agent to draw a card; choose it immediately after placing the Agent and before space or card effects. One Spy cannot pay for both, though different Spies may be used for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence on one placement.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spy Agent icon, Infiltrate, and Gather Intelligence timing and distinct Spy requirement.

answers.answer: Two troops give 4 strength, one sandworm gives 3, and four revealed swords give 4, totaling 11. If your final unit is removed, strength becomes 0. You may play Combat Intrigue only if you have at least one unit in the Conflict, so a player with none cannot participate in that window.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop 2, sandworm 3, sword 1; last unit removed means 0; Combat Intrigue requires a unit.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing does not prevent you from acting again if another player plays a Combat Intrigue; the window ends once all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison), Combat markers reset to 0, and sandworms return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat: may act after earlier pass; consecutive passes close window; cleanup destinations.

answers.answer: With two tied for first in a four-player Conflict, each gets the second reward; the other players compete for the third reward, but nobody wins or takes the Conflict card. With two tied for first in a three-player Conflict, each gets the second reward and no other reward is given; nobody takes the card. A zero-strength player gets no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: exactly two tied first in 4 players leaves others competing for third; 3 or fewer no other rewards; zero strength no reward.

answers.answer: Having one or more sandworms doubles rewards once; multiple sandworms do not multiply again, so two do not quadruple rewards. Control of a location and battle icons on won Conflict cards are not doubled. For a reward of 3 spice to gain 1 VP, you may pay a second 3 spice for a second VP; that uses 6 spice for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: one or more worms double; control and battle icons excluded; repeat optional reward cost.

answers.answer: After winning a Conflict and taking its card face up into your supply, check for another face-up Conflict or Objective card with the same battle icon; if present, you must flip the matching pair face down and gain 1 VP. In the Endgame, a wild icon may match any one of the three icons in your supply and is also resolved for 1 VP. Normal matching is mandatory, not optional.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: matching pair is mandatory; eligible cards; wild match during Endgame.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; falling below 2 loses that VP, and reaching 2 again regains it. At 4, take the printed track bonus, which is retained after falling below 4 and earned again upon returning to 4. The first to 4 takes the Alliance and its 1 VP. A challenger merely tying the holder does not take it; rising above transfers it, with the former holder losing and new holder gaining 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Victory Points, Faction Influence: separate 2-Influence VP, retained 4-track bonus, and temporary Alliance VP.

answers.answer: During the Reveal turn you can use Persuasion before, between, or after Reveal effects to acquire Imperium Row cards or either Reserve card, at the cost shown at the card's top right. You may pool Persuasion from sources to buy one card or split one source across cards; unused Persuasion is lost. The Row refills immediately, so you may buy a replacement if able. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: sources, timing, pooling/splitting, refill, discard destination.

answers.answer: Each Agent-free Maker space receives one bank spice in its bonus spot during Makers, accumulating across rounds; a visit gains all bonus spice there. Deep Desert costs 3 water and gives 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, two sandworms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and gives 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one worm. Worms cannot go in a garrison and cannot be summoned to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery or Imperial Basin while the Shield Wall remains. Hooks are required only when an effect specifies them and are retained, not spent. Removing the Wall allows summoning at any Conflict.
answers.evidence: Makers; Sandworms; Board Space Guide: Deep Desert and Hagga Basin choices and costs.

answers.answer: Endgame is triggered at Recall, at the end of a round, if any player has 10 or more VP or the Conflict Deck is empty. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues, then the most VP wins. The printed resource tiebreakers are spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Phase 5 Recall and Scoring: end trigger, Endgame Intrigue, VP and tiebreak sequence.

answers.answer: CHOAM is optional and Shaddam is optional. With no Shaddam, shuffle all 20 standard contracts, expose two face up and leave 18 in the bank face down. If Shaddam is chosen, set aside both Sardaukar contracts first; shuffle the remaining 18, expose two and leave 16 in the bank, with the two set-aside contracts reserved. Shuffle four additional Intrigue cards into the Intrigue Deck and four additional Imperium cards into the Imperium Deck. The ten contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts stay in the box and are not part of standard setup.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup changes; contrasting-back contracts are separate Rise of Ix compatibility set.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, a contract icon takes one of the two face-up contracts into your supply and replaces it from the bank face up; without CHOAM, it gives 2 Solari. If all contracts have been taken by players, the icon reverts to 2 Solari. A Harvest contract completes when an Agent visits a Maker space and the player gains its shown spice amount that turn in total; Immediate completes upon taking it; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Taking contracts and Completing contracts; shared contract-icon rule in Board Space Guide.

answers.answer: No. If you take a contract for the space after already sending your Agent there that turn, you must wait for a future turn; you must hold it when sending the Agent. On completion announce it, gain its shown rewards, flip it face down, and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts: must hold at Agent placement; announce, gain rewards, flip face down in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. The Rival gets the Ornithopter Objective; humans randomly receive the other two eligible Objectives, and the human whose card shows First Player takes that marker. Turn order each round is First Player → Rival → other human. First Player alternates only between humans. The Rival takes Agent turns but never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: standard 2P setup and Agent turns.

answers.answer: If an indicated destination is occupied, ignore it and reveal another Hagal card. A Place Spy card places a Spy at an empty specified-type post if possible; it does not place an Agent, and whether or not it places a Spy, reveal another card and continue that Agent turn. Ignore ordinary space costs and effects; apply only Hagal effects. If the Hagal deck empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: occupied spaces, Place Spy, ignored space costs/effects, Reshuffle.

answers.answer: For standard 3–4 player setup, shuffle Objective cards after removing those marked for a different player count; distribute one random eligible Objective face up to each player. The player whose Objective bears the First Player marker starts. Shaddam may be chosen only when using the CHOAM Module.
answers.evidence: Setup: omit mismatched Objectives, deal face up, marker selects First Player; Shaddam restriction.

answers.answer: The bank resources and sandworms are not limited; use a convenient substitution if they run out. Troops are limited by a player's supply: if it is empty, that player cannot recruit until troops return there. Gain Solari, spice, and water from the bank; payments are returned to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup bank: not limited; troop recruitment; gains and payments use bank.

answers.answer: The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal the top Conflict card face up, resolve any defensive troop bonus, then each player draws five cards from their own deck. At Recall, if Endgame is not triggered, humans return Agents to Leaders; with 3–4 humans pass First Player clockwise, and in 2P return Rival Agents to its supply and pass First Player to the other human, then start the next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: five phases and Round Start/Recall procedures.

answers.answer: Yes, once the entry cost is paid and requirements are met, the board-space effects, Agent-box effects, and Influence advance may be resolved in any order. No: entry costs and requirements must be met before resolving any effects, so Influence from the visit cannot satisfy its own entry requirement.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs and meet requirements first; then effects may be in any order.

answers.answer: An optional arrow cost/effect can be paid only once per turn, so it cannot normally be repeated. Effects are generally mandatory except where marked “may,” optional arrow costs, and the optional black-X trash icon; direct instructions to trash a card itself are mandatory. Intrigue conditions and costs must be met to play it.
answers.evidence: Arrows / paying costs; FAQ & Rulings: mandatory effects and costs.

answers.answer: A Spy icon places one of your Spies from supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have no Spies in supply when you need one, you may first recall one of your Spies for no effect. If an effect specifies an Agent-icon type connected to the post, you must satisfy that connection or cannot place the Spy.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: empty post, recall if supply empty, specified Agent icon condition.

answers.answer: No. Infiltrate bypasses another player's Agent, not your own. Recalling a Spy requires playing a card for an Agent turn; a Spy does not replace the card requirement. You cannot recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement, though one may be used for Infiltrate and another for Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts and FAQ: Infiltrate limitations and Spy recalls.

answers.answer: The controller gains the separate bonus when any player, including the controller, visits: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, 1 spice at Imperial Basin. Winning the corresponding Conflict gives control by placing your Control marker on the space's flag and replacing an opponent's marker. When its Conflict is revealed, its controller may deploy one troop from their supply directly to the Conflict without an Agent visit.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control: visit bonuses, control by winning, defensive troop from supply.

answers.answer: If two players tie for second in a three-player Conflict, each gets the third reward; the winner keeps the first reward and Conflict card, and no further rewards are given. Players tied for third get nothing. If three players tie for first, each gets the second reward, nobody wins or takes the Conflict card, and no other rewards are given, including in a four-player game.
answers.evidence: Combat ties and Three tied for first table.

answers.answer: In a three-player game with three distinct positive strengths, first and second place receive their printed rewards and third gets nothing. This player-count rule includes two humans plus a scoring Rival: ordinary first and second receive rewards, with the third reward available only in a tie for second.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: player-count reward ranks; Rival section includes two humans plus Rival.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues during Combat only if you have a unit in the Conflict; Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep Intrigues face down, separate from your deck, and reveal only when played; after resolution place them face up in the Intrigue discard pile. If the Intrigue Deck empties, shuffle its discard to form a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards; FAQ Draw timing: Intrigue discard reshuffle.

answers.answer: An ordinary discard instruction discards a card of your choice from your hand and cannot discard an Intrigue unless specified. The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. Secrets makes each opponent with four or more Intrigues give one selected at random.
answers.evidence: Discarding; Intrigue cards: steal Intrigue icon; trash-an-Intrigue icon.

answers.answer: Some effects trash cards from your hand, discard pile, or in play. Return ordinary trashed cards to the box and Reserve cards to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless paying a cost or the card instructs you to trash itself. Trashing The Spice Must Flow does not remove its acquired VP; that VP is retained.
answers.evidence: Trashing; FAQ Victory: acquire VP retained if card later trashed.

answers.answer: Acquire-box effects resolve once when the card is acquired, not later when played. When you cannot draw because your deck is empty, reshuffle your discard pile to form a new deck and continue drawing. Unused Persuasion cannot be saved or carried to another round; it is lost after Reveal.
answers.evidence: Acquire box; Acquiring Cards: reshuffle and unused Persuasion lost.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and cards revealed on your Reveal turn remain face up and in play until Clean Up, unless trashed first. Fremen Bond can use one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards may activate one another regardless of play order. They cease being in play when moved to the discard pile at Clean Up.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond: definition and Clean Up timing.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent just sent this turn; you may use the recalled Agent on a later Agent turn in the same round. Retreat moves a troop from Conflict to your garrison. “Retreat any number” includes zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ Combat and troops.

answers.answer: A free-choice gain-two Influence effect chooses one Faction for both, so it cannot be split. An Alliance icon requires holding that Faction's Alliance token; a minimum-Influence effect requires the specified minimum Influence with that Faction.
answers.evidence: Influence: free choice gains two cannot choose different Factions; Alliance and minimum requirements.

answers.answer: If the holder loses Influence after having been tied, one formerly tied opponent takes the Alliance; if several were tied, the former holder chooses its recipient. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4 or more, return the Alliance token to the board and the former holder loses its 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Victory Points and FAQ Alliance loss: formerly tied recipient; return to board at no 4+ holder.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used this turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, in addition to the normal five cards drawn then. A Plot Intrigue played earlier whose effect applies at Reveal stays face up until that effect is used, then is discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ Draw timing: during Reveal, after Reveal, Plot Intrigue later Reveal effect.

answers.answer: No. A “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first, because nobody wins. If you receive it as a reward for an outright win, you may play it immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ Combat and troops: winning Intrigues cannot follow tie; reward card may be played immediately.

answers.answer: If VP and all four resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed track's 12.
answers.evidence: FAQ Victory: all four tiebreakers tied; scores may exceed 12.

answers.answer: No. Fulfill all contracts held for the same space with one Agent placement; you must hold each contract when sending that Agent. Contract completion is another effect of that Agent turn and may resolve in any order with the space and Agent-box effects.
answers.evidence: FAQ Contract completion: all same-space contracts with one placement; resolve in any order.

answers.answer: Shaddam does not begin with the two reserved Sardaukar contracts. Set both aside before the initial contract shuffle; when acquiring a contract, only Shaddam may choose a reserved one instead of a generally available contract. His Signet Ring deployment restriction takes effect immediately when he plays Signet Ring to send an Agent and lasts for that turn, not the whole round.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Reserved Sardaukar contracts; Shaddam Signet benefits; FAQ Shaddam.

answers.answer: Feyd's token starts on the leftmost space of the Training track and remains on the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica's side begins face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica's side. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: Feyd, Lady Jessica; FAQ: Reverend Mother Jessica.

answers.answer: Yes. Moving from 1 to 3 counts as reaching 2, and the same Faction can reach 2 again later after losing Influence and moving back up; descending through 2 does not count as reaching it. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild's Favor from play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: Margot/Irulan reaching 2; Spacing Guild's Favor Clean Up.

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses Spice Trade access and is not a Faction, so it gives no automatic Influence; it always draws one card and its contract icon gives 2 Solari without CHOAM, takes a face-up contract with CHOAM if available, or gives 2 Solari if none remain. Dutiful Service uses Emperor access, automatically gains one Emperor Influence (count it once), and resolves the same contract icon. Neither has an entry cost or is a Combat space.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: faction status and shared contract-icon rule; table entries.

answers.answer: Arrakeen uses City access, has no cost, and is a Combat space; its visitor recruits one troop and draws one card, while its controller gains 1 Solari. Fremkit uses Fremen access, has no cost, is a Combat space, and gives 1 Fremen Influence and a card. Research Station uses City access, costs 2 water, is a Combat space, and recruits two troops and draws two cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table: Arrakeen, Fremkit, Research Station.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water; its base-spice option is 4 spice, or with Maker Hooks you can choose two sandworms. Hagga Basin costs 1 water; its base-spice option is 2 spice, or with Hooks you can choose one sandworm. Either Maker visit also gains all accumulated bonus spice regardless of choosing worms. Hooks are retained, not spent, when summoning.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Maker space options; Sandworm rules: Hooks not spent.

answers.answer: Both options require City access and at least 2 Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. Option one takes Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruits one troop, and gains 1 water. Option two gains 1 water and may remove the Shield Wall; it does not give a troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Sietch Tabr options and requirements.

answers.answer: High Council uses Landsraad access, costs 5 Solari each visit, and is not a Combat space. First visit places your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and grants 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Subsequent visits give 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: High Council row.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone gains one and 6 Solari after anyone has one; each player may take it only once. Take the third Agent from beside the board to your Leader; it is available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival getting Swordmaster also lowers the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Swordmaster row.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege uses Landsraad access, requires 2 or more Emperor Influence, and costs 3 Solari. Its effects let you discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue, recall one of your other Agents, and draw a card. It does not automatically grant Emperor Influence and cannot recall the Agent sent this turn.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Imperial Privilege; Recall Agent clarification.

answers.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade access, requires at least 2 Spacing Guild Influence, and costs 3 spice. It gains 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; that free-choice Influence need not be Guild Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Shipping row.

answers.answer: Gather Support uses Landsraad access, is not a Combat space, and offers a choice of paying 0 or 2 Solari: recruit two troops either way, and if you pay 2 also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery uses City access, is a Combat space, and offers 0 or 1 spice cost: gain 2 Solari for free, or 4 Solari if you pay 1 spice; its controller separately gains 1 Solari on each visit.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Gather Support and Spice Refinery rows.

answers.answer: Heighliner uses Spacing Guild access, costs 5 spice, gains 1 Guild Influence and recruits five troops; it is a Combat space. Desert Tactics uses Fremen access, costs 1 water, gains 1 Fremen Influence, recruits one troop, and may trash a card; it is a Combat space. Sardaukar uses Emperor access, costs 4 spice, gains 1 Emperor Influence, draws an Intrigue, and recruits four troops; it is not a Combat space. Normal deployment is allowed only at Heighliner and Desert Tactics.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table: Heighliner, Desert Tactics, Sardaukar.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall uses Landsraad access, costs nothing, is not a Combat space, draws an Intrigue, and gives 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn if your Agent is there. Espionage uses Bene Gesserit access, costs 1 spice, is not Combat, and gives 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draws a card, and places a Spy. Deliver Supplies uses Spacing Guild access, costs nothing, is not Combat, and gives 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Assembly Hall, Espionage, Deliver Supplies.

answers.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn. It may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear's red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ: False Orders and Litany Against Fear.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If it is still unacquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ: Manipulate ruling.

answers.answer: The standard Rival starts with a color, four Influence cubes at the bottom of tracks, three troops in garrison and remaining troops in supply, two Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside the board, three Spies and 1 water in supply; score and Combat marker start at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and retain its 2P Reshuffle card. It is a scoring Rival: its 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall and it can win.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: setup; Rival can win and trigger Endgame.

answers.answer: When its Solari, spice, Intrigue cards, and water total reaches its printed Swordmaster threshold, the Rival immediately spends exactly that many resources and takes the third Agent for use that round. Count each unit or Intrigue card as one, including its starting water. Spend mandatory priority order: Solari, then spice, then Intrigue cards, then water, using each type fully as needed and keeping leftovers after the threshold is met. The new Agent is immediately usable.
answers.evidence: Swordmaster resource total and mandatory spending priority.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, each set of exactly 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water is spent for 1 VP. It cannot combine a mixed total of seven different resources for a VP; only the listed exact sets score.
answers.evidence: After Swordmaster: specified resource sets for 1 VP.

answers.answer: For choosing Influence, the Rival selects the Faction where it has least Influence and breaks ties by leftmost priority icon. It gains 1 VP on reaching 2 and handles Alliance VP/transfers like a human, but does not receive the resource bonus for reaching 4. A numbered Hagal Influence icon means the Faction at that position in the Rival card's priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat and resource rules; numbered Influence icon definition.

answers.answer: No. On a two-destination card, use only the destination selected by the current condition; if it is occupied, reveal a new card rather than using the other destination. Guild Influence selects Accept Contract or Shipping; Conflict tier selects Deliver Supplies or Heighliner.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: two-destination selection conditions.

answers.answer: Yes. At every Rival Combat space deploy up to two available garrison troops even if the card recruited none. At a noncombat space, troops recruited by the card go to garrison. A conditional 2+ Influence bonus is simply omitted if unmet; it never prevents the Agent placement.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: troop deployment and conditional bonus.

answers.answer: Unless a post type is specified, place a Spy at the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. Placing the Rival's third and final supply Spy immediately recalls its other two Spies and triggers its Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Spies and Schemes: post priority, third Spy Scheme, no Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence.

answers.answer: Troops recruited by the Scheme before the Agent placement can deploy if the Rival then visits a Combat space that same turn. A Place Spy card with no legal post is ignored, but it still has not sent an Agent, so reveal another Hagal card and continue the Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Spies and Schemes; Place Spy card rule.

answers.answer: The Rival always collects all bonus spice at a visited Maker space. At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, if it has Hooks and worms are permitted at that Conflict, it summons one or two worms respectively instead of taking the base spice; if it summons none, it takes the space's base spice (2 or 4). Without Hooks or at a protected Conflict where worms cannot be summoned, it takes the base spice. Imperial Basin always gives 1 base spice. Accumulated bonus spice is collected in all cases.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces; Sandworm Shield Wall protection.

answers.answer: At the beginning of Combat, if the Rival has at least one deployed unit, reveal one Hagal card in turn order and add its bottom swords as strength. If Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have their normal Combat Intrigue window. A Rival with no deployed unit gets no bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat: reveal Hagal sword bonus before humans' Intrigue window.

answers.answer: Yes: it receives control bonuses, defensive troops, battle-icon VP, normal placement rewards, and reward doubling with one or more sandworms. It always takes an optional Conflict VP if it can pay the resources or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; a contract reward gives it 2 Solari even with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat: control, defensive troop, battle-icon VP, optional VP, contract rule.

answers.answer: During Resolve Reveal Effects, total and announce Combat strength and set the Combat marker at any point while resolving, updating it as needed during the Reveal turn. If strength exceeds 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again at the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn timing; Strength over 20 marker instruction.

answers.answer: The Leader's Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns, not merely when you reveal it. Cards of any type can override the usual rules of the game.
answers.evidence: Setup Leader abilities; Overview: cards of any type can override usual rules.

answers.answer: A Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as the cost for a powerful effect. It is not automatically Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate no-card recall choices and require their own conditions/effects.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Recall Spy icon contrasted with no-card effects.

answers.answer: The trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction discards a card of your choice from your hand and cannot discard an Intrigue unless it explicitly allows it.
answers.evidence: Trashing: separate trash-an-Intrigue icon; Discarding rule.

answers.answer: Yes. Sandworm doubling permits paying the optional cost a second time to gain the second reward; the doubled reward example allows 2 Influence with the same Faction or two different Factions. This differs from one effect that says gain two Influence with free choice: both points must go to one Faction.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling example; Influence free-choice two-gain rule.

answers.answer: Resolve the Rival card's printed Signet Ring ability, not its Scheme. The trigger is a Hagal effect showing the Signet Ring icon; it requires neither a human Signet Ring card nor a Rival Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Rival Signet Ring and Scheme table.

answers.answer: A Maker Hooks icon gives the Rival one token if it has none; if it already has Hooks, it takes no second token. Shield Wall removal works only if the Rival has Hooks and the Wall remains; without Hooks it is ignored, and if the Wall is already gone it has no further effect.
answers.evidence: Rival Hooks and Wall icons table.

answers.answer: Secrets uses Bene Gesserit access, has no entry cost, and is not a Combat space. It gives 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draws an Intrigue from the Intrigue Deck. Separately, each opponent with at least four Intrigues gives you one selected at random.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Secrets; Intrigue steal rule.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade access, has no cost, and is a Combat space. The visitor gains 1 base spice plus all bonus spice there. Its controller separately gains 1 spice, including when the visitor and controller are the same player.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: controlled locations and Imperial Basin row.

answers.answer: Reveal the new Conflict face up next to the deck, on top of any Conflict cards remaining from previous rounds; unclaimed cards remain there. Then resolve any defensive troop bonus before each player draws five cards from their own deck.
answers.evidence: Phase 1 Round Start: reveal Conflict, defensive bonus, then five-card draw.

answers.answer: Each human places one cube on the bottom space of each of the four Faction Influence tracks. Alliance tokens start on the marked areas of the four tracks; no human starts holding one. The Shield Wall token starts in the marked area below Spice Refinery.
answers.evidence: Setup: Shield Wall and Alliance token positions; player cubes at bottom of tracks.

answers.answer: The human with the First Player marker takes the first turn; play proceeds clockwise one turn at a time. A player who Reveals is skipped for the rest of the phase; in standard 3–4 player play, Player Turns ends once all players have Revealed. Combat Intrigue priority starts with First Player and goes clockwise. Each eligible player may play any number of Combat Intrigues or pass; the window closes after all involved players pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Player Turns; Combat Intrigue order and consecutive-pass closure.

answers.answer: The three steps are Reveal Cards (reveal remaining hand), Resolve Reveal Effects (gain those cards' Reveal boxes, use Persuasion, total and set Combat strength), and Clean Up (move all cards in front of you to discard). Reveal effects may be resolved in any order, not necessarily card order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn: three ordered steps and effects in any order.

answers.answer: Shuffle each human's 10-card starter and place it face down in their supply left of the Leader. Without CHOAM, omit CHOAM-marked cards; shuffle the Intrigue and Imperium decks separately face down, then deal five face-up cards from Imperium as the Row; place Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. Human Combat marker starts at 0; three Spies, Councilor and Control markers start in the player's supply; four Influence cubes start at the bottom of the tracks.
answers.evidence: Setup initial deck/card states and player component placement.

answers.answer: Ordinary Persuasion buys any of the five Imperium Row cards, Prepare the Way, or The Spice Must Flow; each card's cost is shown at top right. Make these purchases during your Reveal turn, before, between, or after Reveal effects while spending Persuasion.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: eligible cards, top-right cost, Reveal timing.

answers.answer: Yes. Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional even when a legal action exists. Shield Wall detonation/removal is optional (“may remove”). Once removed, it returns to the box and cannot return in a later round.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: actions optional; Shield Wall rules: remove token, gone for game.

answers.answer: The played card needs an Agent icon matching the destination's upper-left icon, unless that card's Spy Agent icon applies to a connected post where you have a Spy. A Spy connected to Shipping does not let a card with only City icon send an Agent there. If the card has the Spy Agent icon, it may send the Agent to any space connected to a post where you have your Spy, without recalling it.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn card-icon requirement; Spy Agent icon rule.

answers.answer: Yes. On your Agent turn you may first play a legal Plot Intrigue before placing the Agent; resources it grants before entry can pay the destination cost. Resources from the card played to send the Agent or from the destination are gained only after placement, so cannot pay that same entry cost.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot pre-entry gains count; post-placement effects cannot pay entry.

answers.answer: No. In two-player play, after both humans Reveal, continue the Rival's Agent turns while it still has Agents in supply. Proceed to Combat only after both humans have Revealed and the Rival has used all its Agents. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: special 2P completion condition; Rival never Reveals.

answers.answer: When a Conflict is revealed for a space the human already controls, the controller may deploy one troop from their supply directly to the Conflict, without an Agent visit. After rewards, all Combat markers reset to 0 before Makers.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control; Resolve Combat cleanup.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up in front of you and send one Agent from your Leader to an unoccupied matching board space; resolve the Agent box, not its Reveal box. You cannot reuse a card already in play or in your discard pile, nor simply move an Agent already on the board; the ordinary turn uses a card from hand and an Agent from your Leader.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: play from hand, Agent from Leader, Agent box; card and placement rules.

answers.answer: The restriction applies immediately when Shaddam plays Signet Ring to send an Agent, so he cannot deploy units that turn. The general freedom to order board-space and Agent-box effects cannot postpone the restriction until after deployment.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: Shaddam restriction takes effect immediately.

answers.answer: With four different positive strengths, first, second and third receive their respective printed rewards; fourth receives none. The highest-strength player wins and takes the Conflict card face up, then checks for a battle-icon match.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: 4-player rank rewards and winner takes card.

answers.answer: Players may choose Leaders or select them at random; random distribution is not required.
answers.evidence: Setup: each player takes a Leader (choose, or select at random).

answers.answer: An ordinary draw-a-card effect draws from your own deck, reshuffling your own discard pile if needed. You may not choose a card directly from your discard pile instead.
answers.evidence: Drawing cards: ordinary draw is from your own deck, not a chosen discard card.

answers.answer: Shuffle the House Hagal deck and place it near the shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card in the deck; it is not removed.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules setup: shuffle House Hagal and retain 2P Reshuffle card.

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks tokens begin in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human. A token later acquired moves from the bank onto that player's garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup: Maker Hooks tokens in bank; acquired token moves onto player's garrison.

answers.answer: Yes. If a Combat Intrigue changes deployed units or otherwise alters strength, adjust the Combat marker when the card resolves during the Combat Intrigue window. The Reveal-turn value is not fixed until cleanup; rewards use the adjusted strength shown on the track after all involved players pass.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: adjust marker on resolution; Combat resolved using adjusted track strength.

answers.answer: Gained Solari, spice, or water comes from the common bank. You do not take resources from another player's supply; payments return resources to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup bank: gains from bank, payments returned to bank.

answers.answer: Shuffle the 20 standard contract tokens face down before exposing two face up offers; place the remaining tokens face down in the bank. Players do not choose the offers or preset the hidden bank order. If Shaddam is chosen, first set aside both Sardaukar contracts, then shuffle the other 18 before exposing two and banking 16.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup changes: shuffle contracts face down, then flip two; Shaddam setup exception.

answers.answer: Before shuffling, set aside both Sardaukar contracts. Only Shaddam can acquire them, and setting them aside does not give him possession. Shuffle the other 18 standard contracts, expose two face up and put 16 face down in the bank; the two reserved Sardaukar contracts remain set aside.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup changes and Reserved Sardaukar contracts.
